note.explanation: Friction is a force that opposes motion between surfaces. It can slow moving objects and change some of their energy into heat. The main types in this section are static friction, kinetic friction and rolling friction.
examples: A cricket ball slows down on the ground because friction acts opposite to its motion.
A wheel rolls more easily than an object slides because rolling friction is much smaller than sliding friction.
note.simple: Friction is a force that resists motion. It can slow things down, warm surfaces, and make it harder for objects to slide.
note.checkQuestion: What is the constant velocity reached when air resistance balances gravity called?
note.title: Friction and its effects
steps: Identify the surfaces or fluid involved.
Decide whether the object is at rest, sliding, rolling or falling through air.
Name the friction or resistance acting on it.
State how that force affects the object's motion.
note.answer: Friction opposes motion. Static friction acts before surfaces start sliding; kinetic friction acts while they slide; rolling friction acts while an object rolls. Air resistance can balance gravity and produce terminal velocity.

rationales: This is right because static friction acts before the surfaces start sliding.
This is wrong because kinetic friction acts when surfaces are sliding.
This is wrong because rolling friction acts when an object rolls over a surface.
This is wrong because air resistance is not the friction holding the block at rest on the table.

mcqs.stem: What happens when the applied pull on a stationary block exceeds the limit of static friction?
rationales: This is right because the block begins to slide once the limiting static friction is overcome.
This is wrong because exceeding static friction does not by itself make the block roll.
This is wrong because forces, including kinetic friction, still act on the block.
This is wrong because the applied pull does not change the block's weight.

options: The object's speed keeps increasing

mcqs.stem: What happens when a falling object reaches terminal velocity?
rationales: This is wrong because the object stops accelerating when the forces balance.
This is right because balanced air resistance and gravity leave the object falling at constant velocity.
This is wrong because gravity continues to act downward.
This is wrong because balanced forces do not make the object reverse direction.

rationales: This is wrong because the section says rolling friction is smaller.
This is right because the section states that rolling friction is about one hundred times smaller.
This is wrong because the two types of friction are not stated to be equal.

written.text: Define terminal velocity of an object.
written.finalAnswer: The constant velocity achieved by an object when air resistance balances the downward force of gravity is called its terminal velocity.

rubric.why: The definition requires the forces that balance at terminal velocity.
rubric.how: State that air resistance balances the downward force of gravity.

rubric.why: Terminal velocity is identified by the object's constant speed of falling.

modelAnswer: A speed is finally attained at which the upward force of air resistance balances the downward force of gravity.
When this happens, the object stops accelerating and keeps falling at a constant velocity.
This constant velocity achieved by an object is called its terminal velocity.

written.finalAnswer: Friction between tyres and the road helps vehicles move and provides the force needed for braking. Spaces in the tyre tread pattern prevent a wet layer forming between tyre and road, reducing the chances of skidding on wet roads.

examTips: This section is tested mainly through short definitions, explanations of everyday examples, and comprehensive questions about a block on a table or friction in vehicles.
For a definition question, use the textbook's key terms: opposing force, static friction, kinetic friction, rolling friction and constant velocity.
For the block question, explain the sequence: pull applied, static friction opposes it, limiting static friction is reached, then the block slides and kinetic friction acts.
For terminal velocity, state both that air resistance balances gravity and that the object then falls at constant velocity.
For vehicle questions, connect friction to grip and braking, and mention the tyre tread's role in reducing skidding on wet roads.

explain.title: Friction opposes motion and dissipates energy
explain.body: Friction is a dissipative force due to which the energy is wasted in doing work to overcome against friction. The lost energy appears in the form of heat. For example, rubbing hands makes them warm, and friction can heat and wear vehicle tyres.

explain.title: Static and kinetic friction
explain.body: The friction between two solid surfaces is called sliding friction which can be divided into two categories. Static friction acts when a pull tends to move an object but it remains at rest. When the object slides, the friction is known as kinetic friction.

explain.title: Terminal velocity
explain.body: As a falling object gets faster, air resistance increases. When the upward force of air resistance balances the downward force of gravity, the object stops accelerating and keeps falling at a constant velocity. This constant velocity achieved by an object is called its terminal velocity.

explain.title: Rolling friction and reducing friction
explain.body: When an object rolls over a surface, the friction produced is called rolling friction. Rolling friction is about one hundred times smaller than sliding friction. Friction can also be reduced by polishing surfaces, applying oil or grease, using ball bearings and making moving bodies streamlined.

mistakes: Do not say static friction acts only when no force is applied; it opposes a force that tends to move a stationary object.
Do not call the friction on a sliding block static friction; once the block slides, it is kinetic friction.
Do not define terminal velocity as a speed reached when gravity stops acting; gravity still acts and is balanced by air resistance.
Do not confuse rolling friction with sliding friction; rolling friction is much smaller.
Do not say tyre tread removes friction; its spaces help prevent a wet layer and reduce the chance of skidding.
In a question about a falling object, mention both balanced forces and constant velocity to earn the full definition marks.
